PC: Sanitizes hands upon entering the room
Begins the HPI with open-ended questions
Sanitizes hands at the end of the encounter on the way out
SBP: The student ended the encounter with a clear plan for next steps (this does not necessarily mean that the patient and student decided which of the two treatment courses to pursue).a
ICS: Knocks and enters the room
Shakes hands and **introduces self** by first and last name
Asks patient how they would like to be addressed, including formal title
Negotiates agenda/focus of visit
Elicits patient's perspective and beliefs (fears, concerns, ideas)
Facilitates the storytelling by saying, "Tell me more"
Uses nonverbal skills to demonstrate that they are attentive and present (brings Kleenex)
Maintains eye contact
Speaks clearly and audibly
Demonstrates active listening (includes non-verbals, headnodding, posture)
Demonstrates empathy when appropriate throughout the encounter
Avoids using medical jargon, or explains jargon throughout the encounter
Adjusts tone and pacing as appropriate throughout the encounter
Creates a mutual understanding of the patient’s prognosis
Delivers the bad news in very plain language, slowly and carefully
Allows for silence as appropriate
Responds appropriately to the patient's emotions
Gives information in small amounts
Effectively communicates both known details and uncertainty
Assures the patient that the medical team would continue to help the patient
Asks about the patient’s significant relationships/support system
Offers to partner with the patient in having difficult conversations with family
Considers cultural and other factors that influence the patient’s understanding of illness/diagnosis
The student elicited the patient’s religious and/or spiritual beliefs and, if appropriate, incorporated these beliefs into the discussion.
Elicits the patient’s goals of care (i.e. "at this stage given your understanding of the situation what are your goals?")
Student demonstrated compassion - (i.e. apology followed by 'I wish things were different…')
Sets an agenda of what will be discussed - possible treatment plans
Assesses prior knowledge - 'do you know anyone else who has had this kind of serious diagnosis?' (ASK)
Asks what other information might be helpful (ASK)
Allows time for questions and concerns
Inquires if patient wants to include someone else next visit
Summarizes visit's important points and uses TEACH BACK (i.e. when you are talking to your family tonight and they ask about the visit, what will be your response?)
Thanks the patient and uses one more PEARLS statement to close the visit, before standing upa
Establishes and maintains rapport with the patient
PROF: States that they are a medical student
Asks patient what pronoun should be used when writing clinical note
Demonstrates respect for the patient’s autonomy
The student conducted the encounter with an honest, trustworthy demeanor.a
The student offered false hope that the condition is not imminently terminal.
